title: feat(meta): mask object schemas per caller on every /meta exit (ADR-0106)
body:
Fixes objectstack-ai/objectstack#3682

Implements ADR-0106 (`docs/adr/0106-metadata-plane-fls-object-schema-masking.md`, merged as #3678) — step ③ of #3661. Steps ① ② shipped client-side as objectui#2866; nothing here touches objectui.

Premise re-verified against `origin/main` before writing any code: `grep -n getReadableFields packages/rest/src packages/runtime/src` found exactly one call site, the #3547 export-column projection at `rest-server.ts:6169`. Zero on any `/meta` or `/metadata` read path. The gap was real and total.

---

## The invariant, in one sentence

For a caller who cannot read a field, that field is **completely absent** from every object schema the platform serves — no bare name, no `null`, no 200 with empty `fields`. The metadata plane joins the posture the data plane has had since the #3391 series.

## D1/D2 — projection in the dispatch layer, field removed whole

Serving an object schema projects `fields` onto `security.getReadableFields(object, ctx)`. A field outside the set goes entirely: name, label, type, picklist options, `formula`, `visibleWhen`, `defaultValue`, `requiredPermissions`. Partial redaction was rejected by the ADR — keeping the name still leaks existence and invites ghost columns.

`metadata-protocol` is untouched: `getMetaItem` / `getMetaItems` signatures do not move, which is exactly what keeps D3's single-copy cache sound.

## D5 — one shared projection, called at every outlet

The normalizer lives in `@objectstack/metadata-core` (`object-schema-fls.ts`), by the same criterion `applyAuditFieldGovernance` (#4513) and the engine dispatch predicates (#5619) were sunk there: the exits are split across two dispatch packages, `metadata-core` depends only on `{ spec, zod }`, so there is no new edge and no cycle. `packages/rest` gains it as a dependency.

Following #6561's per-exit shared-normalizer shape, one pure function is called at each exit rather than per-route logic:

**`@objectstack/rest`**
- `GET /meta/:type/:name` — cached branch (the default, `enableCache` defaults true)
- the same route, uncached branch — which is also what `?state=draft`, `?preview=draft`, `?package=` and `enableCache: false` take
- `?layers=true` — the layered diagnostic view, all three of `code` / `overlay` / `effective`
- `GET /meta/:type/:section/:name` — the compound-name read
- `GET /meta/:type` — the list read, each item projected against its own object's posture

**`@objectstack/runtime` (`/metadata` catch-all)**
- the object branch's protocol-backed, registry-backed and last-ditch lookups
- `/metadata/objects` — both the protocol-backed and registry-backed list reads
- the legacy one-segment `/metadata/:objectName` read

The posture is resolved **once** at the top of each handler, from the normalized `metaType` (#3984 / #6241 — a gate keyed on the raw `:type` param is a gate the canonical plural spelling walks past), and every branch below projects through that one value.

> The issue text describes the landing sites as "cached 与非 cached 两条路径". That wording predates #5895's envelope convergence: `translateMetaEnvelope` is now the single rebuild point, and the two branches still differ in *how they reach a document*, so both are still masked — plus the three outlets above that the ADR's enumeration did not name.

## D3 — mask after the cache, fingerprint the ETag

The shared cache keeps storing **one full schema** per (type, name, locale, environment); no caller dimension in the key, so storage stays O(objects). What varies per caller is the validator: a stable FNV-1a hash of the caller's **denied** set, folded into the ETag as `<hash>~<fingerprint>`.

- An unrestricted caller denies nothing → empty fingerprint → the fold is the identity → **ETag and body byte-identical** to post-#6561 `main`.
- Same cohort → same validator → shared `304`s.
- A permission change moves the fingerprint → the stale `304` self-invalidates. Nothing to purge.

One correctness detail worth reviewing: when a projection applies, `If-None-Match` is **not** forwarded to `getMetaItemCached`. Its validator hashes the *unfiltered* document, so a `304` decided there would pin the caller to a body no mask ever touched — the validator-vs-served-body mismatch #5881 recorded for the dashboard gate. The comparison moves down into the REST layer, against the fingerprinted ETag that identifies what is actually being sent. `getMetaItemCached` delegates to `getMetaItem` internally, so this costs no extra work.

The order is stronger than the ADR requires: the posture is resolved **before** the fetch, so on the failure tier the cached document is never even produced. Pinned as measured, because the weaker claim ("we fetched it and then withheld it") would still be satisfied by a refactor that leaks on an early return.

## D4 — exemptions are caller properties

`isSystem`, plus platform admins judged by the same `systemPermissions` reading the `app` filter uses (`studio.access` / `setup.access`). An exempt caller gets the full schema on the public route; a non-exempt caller gets the projection on every route. The exemption short-circuits **before** the security service is consulted, so a sick service cannot fault an admin out of Studio.

## D6 — three tiers, never silent, never empty-200

| Condition | Response |
|---|---|
| no `security` service | serve unmasked — the deployment has no FLS posture at all |
| `getReadableFields` → `undefined` | serve unmasked **+** structured warn **+** `objectstack_meta_field_visibility_undetermined_total` **+** `Cache-Control: private, no-store`, no shared ETag |
| evaluation **throws** | `503 FIELD_VISIBILITY_UNRESOLVED` — never the unmasked body, never an empty-fields 200 |

One judgement call the ADR did not spell out, flagged for review: `getReadableFields` answering `[]` is treated as the **error** tier, not as a 200 with `fields: {}`. `[]` is only ever produced where plugin-security's own posture read failed closed (#3545), and D6 rules an empty-fields 200 out in as many words ("silently wrong UI **and** cacheable poison").

## D7 — zero-permission-set callers

`@objectstack/plugin-security` gains `getMetadataReadableFields`, which differs from `getReadableFields` in exactly one place: a caller resolving to zero permission sets resolves the configured fallback set (`security.fallbackPermissionSet`, default `member_default`) — the same two-step `/auth/me/permissions` performs — instead of falling open.

`getReadableFields` is deliberately unchanged. On the data plane, mirroring the engine middleware's fall-open is what keeps it drift-free; on the metadata plane the question is disclosure, and D7 rules that a public deployment's exposure must be a permission-set decision. The dispatch layer feature-detects the new method and falls back to `getReadableFields`, so a partial implementation degrades rather than lies.

**Contract note (needs a follow-up, see below):** the method is registered as an explicit `Object.assign` extension of the typed `ISecurityService` literal rather than declared on the interface, because `packages/spec` was off this task's file surface.

## D8 — default on, with an escape hatch

Masking is the platform default. Two knobs, one meaning: `metadata.maskObjectFields: false` on the REST server, and `OS_ALLOW_UNMASKED_OBJECT_METADATA=1` deployment-wide (Prime Directive #9's `OS_ALLOW_{X}` escape-hatch shape). The env var exists because the runtime `/metadata` dispatcher has no REST config to read.

The REST config key is read through `(metadata as any)`, following the same precedent as `api.enableOpenApi` / `api.enableSearch` two lines above it — declaring it on `MetadataEndpointsConfigSchema` is a `packages/spec` edit, which was off surface. Recorded as an open question below.

---

## Tests

**One case table, every exit.** `@objectstack/metadata-core/testing` exports `OBJECT_SCHEMA_MASK_CASES` (11 rows: two restricted-projection shapes, unrestricted byte-identity, all three D6 tiers, the empty-readable refusal, both D4 exemptions, D7's fallback, D8's opt-out) plus a framework-free matcher. Both dispatch suites drive **all** of their outlets through it, so an exit that forgets the projection fails **by name** rather than by nobody noticing.

- `packages/rest/src/meta-object-fls.test.ts` — 7 exit groups × 11 cases, plus the D3 ETag block and the D6 wire block: **88 tests**
- `packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-object-fls.test.ts` — 6 resolvers × 11 cases, plus the "a masking fault is not a lookup miss" pin: **67 tests**
- `packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls.test.ts` — the pure module: **21 tests**
- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/get-metadata-readable-fields.test.ts` — D7, asserting **both** methods on every case so the pair can only change together: **7 tests**

The absence assertion is not just "`name` not in `fields`" — it also fails if the name appears **anywhere** in the serialized document, so a partial redaction cannot pass.

### Reverse verification

Predicted **before** running, then measured, by disabling the projection (`applyObjectSchemaMask` returns its input for every posture):

| | predicted red | measured red |
|---|---|---|
| `packages/rest` FLS suite | 28 contract rows (4 projection-dependent × 7 exits) + 2 ETag + 1 empty-projection = **31** | **31 failed / 57 passed** |
| `packages/runtime` FLS suite | 4 projection-dependent rows × 6 resolvers = **24** | **24 failed / 43 passed** |

Exactly as predicted, including the guard rails that had to stay **green**: both D4 exemption rows, all three D6 posture rows, the unrestricted-caller row and the D8 opt-out row — those do not depend on the projection and did not move. Restored, re-run, 88/67 green.

## Gates

Every step enumerated from `.github/workflows/lint.yml`, run one by one — the ESLint job's 22 `check:*` steps and the TypeScript Type Check job's full sequence (root gates, `@objectstack/spec`'s twelve, full-workspace `turbo run typecheck`, the DEBT re-measure, examples, downstream contract, i18n). All green. Full `turbo run test`: 135/135 tasks green.

`check:nul-bytes` caught one real slip on the first pass: the fingerprint separator had been written as a raw NUL byte instead of the escape text. Fixed in its own commit.

Everything was re-run after `git merge origin/main` (through `82397b6`), with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, a full `pnpm build` and `rm -rf packages/runtime/.objectstack` first, per AGENTS.md §9 — including `@objectstack/spec check:generated` (10/10 artifacts current) since the merge moved spec.

## Out-of-scope findings filed (Prime Directive #10)

The D5(4) outlet audit found three things this PR deliberately does not fix. All searched-first, filed unassigned with `finding`:

- **#6603** — after this change, a restricted caller's `GET → edit → PUT` of an object schema **deletes** the fields that were masked out of their read. `PUT /meta/:type/:name` carries no capability gate (the `_migrate` route's own comment says so), and ADR-0106 is **silent** on the round-trip — so the write path is untouched here rather than guessed at. This is the one finding a reviewer should read before merging.
- **#6599** — `/meta/_drafts` and `/metadata/_drafts` serve draft object schemas unmasked. Left out because the prior question is whether the route belongs to non-authors at all; a projection would quietly bless that access.
- **#6601** — a section-less public form publishes every non-server-managed field of its target object to **anonymous** callers (`allowed.size === 0` falls through to all fields).

Checked and **not** outlets: `/openapi.json` (documents "object, shape not described here" — never enumerates fields), OData `$metadata`/describe (no such route exists here; `odata.zod.ts` is a query-adapter spec), the client SDK's describe calls (they proxy REST and inherit the mask), and `/data/:object/export` (already projects columns via #3547).

## Not touched

`packages/spec`, `content/docs/releases/`, `objectui`, the `metadata-protocol` signatures, and the metadata **write** path.
